newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan calls for calm in island sovereignty row.
newsitem.headline: Japan calls for calm in island sovereignty row.

text.p: Japan on Thursday urged China, Taiwan and Hong Kong to deal calmly with a territorial dispute over islands in the East China Sea, as tensions mounted following the rebuilding of a lighthouse by a Japanese right-wing group earlier this week.
"We must deal with the issue calmly," a Foreign Ministry official told Reuters.

A long-dormant sovereignty dispute over the islands, called the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese, erupted in July after the right-wing Japan Youth Federation erected a lighthouse on one of the islands, angering Taiwan and China, which also claim ownership of the islands.

The Japanese official, who declined to be identified, said Tokyo has not been able to confirm Taiwanese media reports that Taipei urged Japanese and Taiwan boats not to fish within 12 miles (20 km) of the uninhabited islands.
"We have not confirmed that Taiwan has made such a proposal," the Japanese official said.
Japan has no diplomatic ties with Taiwan, and recognises its communist rival Beijing instead.
Seeking to resolve the dispute through diplomatic means, Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday it was ready to negotiate with Japan over fishing rights in waters near the islands.

"Because Japan does not have diplomatic ties with Taiwan, there will be no direct talks between the two governments," the Japanese official said. "Japan will convey its views through private channels," he added.
Taiwan had sought a fishery pact with Tokyo at a private meeting in August, he said.
Beijing has warned of serious damage to bilateral ties if Japanese rightists set foot on the islands. Angry Taiwanese legislators urged Taipei to send military forces to the area.
In Hong Kong, daily protests have been staged for more than a week, urging Beijing to take tougher action to protect its territory.
The issue has united Chinese in China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Macau, bringing together groups which are usually at odds with each other.

"The media in Hong Kong and Taiwan have created a perception that the Japanese government and the private group are working together," the Japanese official said. "We want them to understand that that is not true."
The Japanese right-wingers said on Wednesday they built the controversial lighthouse to ensure the safety of ships sailing in the East China Sea.
